lines: If a wildfire traps you in the forest, never seek shelter inside a wooden cabin.
Cole has only 10 minutes before a raging wall of fire engulfs the timber.
Heavy black smoke chokes the dusk air as burning embers shower the winding road.
An evacuation alert sounded earlier, but waiting too long created an extreme survival trap.
One. Leave early when told to evacuate, because waiting is the most dangerous choice.
A small wooden cabin stands ahead, but timber shelters quickly burn to the ground.
Two. If on foot, head immediately for ground with little fuel like bare rock.
Cole turns his back on the wooden cabin and runs toward a granite clearing.
Three. Reach the bare stone surface and crouch down low to escape toxic gases.
Cole drops down flat against the rock, pressing his face to the cold earth.
A massive firestorm slams the treeline, instantly incinerating the wooden cabin in blinding flames.
Screaming winds scatter burning debris, but the barren stone gives the inferno zero fuel.
Cole survived the devastating initial impact because bare mineral ground stopped the advancing blaze.
It was the perfect plan, executed exactly as required during a deadly forest emergency.
There was just one problem that destroyed his only chance of waiting it out.
A massive wall of suffocating radiant heat now forces Cole toward his trapped car.
part1.cliffhanger: Unbearable radiant heat makes the bare rock unlivable, forcing Cole to seek shelter inside his trapped vehicle as flames close in.
